doc.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024

title: Meeting Carla Bley at Billy Tripps in Willow, New York
summary: In 1979 his group played a bar in Willow near Woodstock where Carla Bley noticed him; he cried when she died.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In your bio, one of them, there’s a brief thing about you being, in 1979, in an Upstate New York bar and noticed by jazz pianist Carla Bley. I wonder if you can tell me what the Upstate bar was, because I live in Upstate New York.
I bet you it’s not there. Do you know Willow, New York? Willow, New York is a little hamlet like I want to say 20 minutes from Woodstock. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

It’s basically a post office. It’s basically where Carla had her home. Her home was in Willow and there was the post office and a bar, and the bar was called Billy Tripps. And we were just kids, as I told you before, we were just pot smoking hippie jazz kids and all we wanted to do was play. And somehow we found a way. My friend had a house on Route 212 outside of Willow. And his parents had a house there. And so we found ourselves with a gig at this bar and Carla Bley was one of the people. And you know it’s funny how you don’t think about the things in your life that — Carla Bley went on to have such a huge role in my life. I cried like a baby when she died.
Thank you. I’ve tried. I’ve tried to be of service.
